q_44959.question_text: What will the first reported revenues after June 2026 be for the following companies? (SpaceX)
q_44959.reasoning:
# Analysis of SpaceX Q2 2026 Revenue Forecast

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings report is scheduled for August 4, 2026. Today is July 25, 2026. This means **10 days until resolution**.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The CURRENT RESEARCH provides a highly specific analyst estimate: **Benzinga Pro estimates SpaceX will report quarterly revenue of $6.98 billion** for Q2 2026.

This is a rare case where we have:
1. A concrete, very recent analyst consensus estimate (from major financial data provider Benzinga Pro)
2. The exact reporting date confirmed as August 4, 2026
3. Clear context that this covers only 19 days of operations as a public company (IPO was ~June 11, 2026)

The $6.98 billion estimate should be treated as the market consensus view and represents the most likely outcome. This estimate falls comfortably within the provided range (5.5B - 8.5B).

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Conservative guidance**: If SpaceX's actual underlying business performance was weaker than expected, they might report below consensus
- **Revenue recognition timing**: Questions about when certain contracts are recognized could push reported revenue down
- **Q2 seasonality**: Any unexpected slowdown in the narrow June 30 reporting window
- **Competitive pressures**: Any unforeseen challenges to major customer contracts

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Better-than-expected commercial activity**: Strong Starshield contracts, international launches, or satellite constellation growth
- **Recognition timing**: Revenue recognition for multi-quarter contracts could front-load into Q2
- **Government contracts acceleration**: Additional defense/national security contracts signed before quarter-end
- **Starlink performance**: Better-than-expected commercial or government satellite internet revenues

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

No reliable base rate available from the provided materials. SpaceX has never previously reported public quarterly revenues as a public company. The Benzinga Pro estimate of $6.98 billion is the most concrete data point available and represents professional analyst consensus very close to the resolution date.

---

**Reasoning on probability distribution:**

The Benzinga Pro consensus of $6.98B is essentially our anchor point. With only 10 days until resolution and a highly specific professional estimate, the distribution should be relatively tight around this figure. Historical accuracy of Benzinga consensus estimates is typically good for near-term earnings, particularly for a company of SpaceX's size and visibility.

The range allows for outcomes from <5.5B to >8.5B, which represents roughly ±20% variance from the consensus estimate. Given the information available and the proximity to resolution, I'm centering the distribution around the $6.98B consensus with moderate confidence in the estimate.

Median (50th percentile): 6980000000
High (90th percentile): 8200000000
q_44959.research_text:
SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX) is scheduled to release its first public earnings report for the second quarter of 2026 after market close on Tuesday, August 4, 2026. This will cover the period ending June 30, 2026; a quarter in which SpaceX was a public company for only 19 days [teslaoracle.com](https://www.teslaoracle.com/2026/07/21/spacex-spcx-announces-the-date-for-its-first-ever-earnings-call-and-financial-results-q2-2026/).

Benzinga Pro estimates SpaceX will report a loss of 25 cents per share on quarterly revenue of $6.98 billion [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/07/60612760/quick-spark-spacex-to-report-first-public-earnings-on-august-4-details-and-estimates-inside). Macquarie maintains an Outperform rating and a $250 price target, highlighting SpaceX's potential as an AI infrastructure asset [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/07/60612760/quick-spark-spacex-to-report-first-public-earnings-on-august-4-details-and-estimates-inside).

The earnings call on August 4th will be followed by a significant unlock of early-release eligible shares on August 6th, increasing the tradable float by approximately 920 million shares [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/22/spacex-earnings-are-coming-aug-4/), [starpath.global](https://starpath.global/news/spacex-to-post-first-earnings-as-public-company-on-august-4th/). An additional 10% of shares could be unlocked if the stock averages above $175.50 for five of the ten trading days leading up to August 4th, which is currently unlikely [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/22/spacex-earnings-are-coming-aug-4/), [wetalktesla.com](https://wetalktesla.com/2026/07/21/spacex-august-4-q2-results-ipo-lockup/).
